criterion: The home route uses two page grounds, a near-black neutral and a near-white neutral, meeting at a hard full-width edge.
evaluation_rule: A HARD EDGE means the ground changes at a straight boundary with zero blending between the two tones. Yes if every ground change on the home route is a hard boundary between a near-black tone and a near-white tone. No if a third background tone appears, or if one ground blends into the other.

criterion: Body text on the near-white ground is pure black and body text on the near-black ground is pure white.
evaluation_rule: Yes if reading text on the light ground is pure black and reading text on the dark ground is pure white. No if either is a softened near-black, a grey, or an off-white.

criterion: A single mid, vivid teal marks the pointer dot, the highlight behind selected text and the current chapter in a case rail, always beside a word.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the teal appears in those three places, carries a word beside it wherever it marks position, and appears nowhere else. No if the teal is missing from any of the three, stands alone as the only signal of position, or appears as a button fill, a panel background or a heading colour.

criterion: Error text under a contact form field is a light, muted red reserved for errors alone.
evaluation_rule: Yes if an error message under a contact field is a light, muted red and that red appears nowhere else on the site. No if errors carry a different colour, or that red is reused for something other than an error.

criterion: Four lettering voices divide the work across the site, with a monospaced face carrying every label, caption and address.
evaluation_rule: The FOUR VOICES are a heavy display face, a plain reading face, a light italic serif and a monospace. Yes if all four are distinguishable on the home route and the small supporting text is monospaced. No if fewer than four faces appear, or the labels and captions are set in the same proportional face as the body copy.

criterion: The public routes read as an editorial performance and the engagement portal reads as a quiet working tool.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the marketing routes carry large type and staging while the portal is dense, plain and built for scanning. No if the portal carries the same editorial staging as the marketing routes, or the marketing routes read as an administrative console.

criterion: The engagement portal opens on a single line of text saying what is happening now, above every other panel.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the first thing inside the portal is one line describing the current state of the engagement. No if the portal opens on a list, a table or any panel other than that one line.

criterion: The tone board is a square field carrying two labelled axes, restrained to expressive across and classical to contemporary upward.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the board is square, both axes are labelled at each end, and the four labels read restrained, expressive, classical and contemporary. No if the board is unlabelled, carries one axis only, or uses different words at the ends.

criterion: The home route sits inside a frame of gutter, content column and gutter, under a header band fixed across the full viewport width.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the content is inset from both edges by a matching margin and the header spans the whole width and stays put as the page scrolls. No if the content runs edge to edge, or the header scrolls away with the page.

criterion: Rules on the home route come in three strengths, used to separate structure rather than to decorate.
evaluation_rule: Yes if three distinguishable rule weights appear, each marking a different kind of division. No if every rule on the page carries one weight, or rules appear where nothing is being divided.

criterion: Each client sector count on the home route is ringed by a hand-drawn ellipse whose stroke crosses itself and leaves a gap.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each count carries an irregular ring that overlaps itself and stays open. No if the counts are ringed by a clean closed ellipse, by brackets, or by nothing at all.

criterion: The wide metallic band on the home route reads as brushed metal, carrying one soft bright streak across its upper third.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the band shows fine horizontal grain and a single soft highlight across the upper part. No if it reads as flat grey, as random noise, or carries no highlight.

criterion: A case name rises into place beneath its panel on the home archive as the panel is revealed.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the name travels upward into position as the image above it arrives. No if the name is already in place before the image arrives, or appears with no movement.

criterion: At a phone width a case panel on the archive arrives by fading rather than by a corner wipe.
evaluation_rule: A CORNER WIPE is an edge travelling diagonally across the image. Yes if the phone reveal is a plain fade. No if the phone reveal is the diagonal wipe used on a wide screen.

criterion: The home route, the case archive and the staged brief each lead with one primary action styled apart from every secondary control on that surface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each of those three surfaces carries one action that stands out from the controls around it. No if a surface carries several equally prominent actions, or every control shares one treatment.

criterion: The fixed header stays legible on the home route over both the near-black ground and the near-white ground, rendering as the inverse of whatever passes beneath.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the header wordmark reads clearly over both grounds and appears as the inverse of the ground under it, dark over the light ground and light over the dark ground. No if the wordmark becomes unreadable over either ground, or keeps one fixed colour whatever lies beneath.

criterion: Major headings pair a heavy geometric roman with a lighter italic serif, set on line boxes shorter than the letter height.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a major heading shows both lettering styles together and its lines sit closer than the height of the letters. No if headings use a single lettering style, or the lines are spaced at or above the letter height.

criterion: Pressable controls are full stadiums, panels are softly rounded rectangles and discipline tags are barely rounded, every surface sitting flat against the page.
evaluation_rule: Yes if all three roundness tiers are visibly different from one another and every surface is separated by rules, ground changes or spacing alone. No if controls, panels and tags share one rounding, or any surface carries a drop shadow.

criterion: Elements arriving on the home route decelerate into position over a visible settle.
evaluation_rule: Yes if elements that appear as the page is scrolled slow down as they land. No if they appear at once, or travel at one speed and stop dead.

criterion: A tone tile released onto the board carries momentum, settling just past the point where the pointer let go.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the tile overshoots the release point a little and returns. No if the tile stops dead where the pointer released it.

criterion: With motion reduced the site keeps its layout, its ground changes and its heading pairings, losing only the travel.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the site with motion reduced shows the same arrangement, the same hard ground changes and the same paired headings, every element resting in its final position. No if it becomes a plain unstyled page, or content stays hidden because a reveal was skipped.

criterion: The small mark beside the wordmark turns as a set of rings moving against one another.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the mark shows more than one ring and at least one ring turns opposite to another. No if the whole mark rotates as a single piece.

criterion: Body text meets the WCAG AA contrast bar against both the near-black ground and the near-white ground.
evaluation_rule: Yes if reading text clears the AA bar on both grounds. No if text on either ground falls below it.

criterion: A visible focus ring follows the keyboard through the home route in reading order, staying visible as focus crosses the header.
evaluation_rule: Yes if tabbing moves a visible ring from control to control in the order the page reads, and the ring stays visible over the header. No if focus becomes invisible anywhere, or the order jumps around the page.

criterion: At a phone width the pointer replacement is absent and every control on the home route stays large enough to press with a fingertip.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the system pointer behaviour returns on a touch screen and the tags, links and controls are comfortably pressable. No if a custom pointer is drawn on a touch screen, or a control is too small to press reliably.

criterion: The band of four numbered capabilities scrolls as an ordinary section at a phone width rather than holding still.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the capability band moves with the page on a phone. No if the band is held in place on a phone as the items advance past.

criterion: A route of the site shows large blocks of body text that stay invisible after the page has settled.
evaluation_rule: Yes if any route leaves a block of body copy invisible once the page has settled. No if all body copy is readable once the page has settled.

criterion: The capabilities deck arrives as a document file to download rather than as a page at its own address.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the deck flow ends in the download of a document file. No if the deck opens as a page at its own address.

criterion: The header wordmark jumps to a new appearance in one step as the ground beneath changes on the home route.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the wordmark visibly flicks as the boundary between the two grounds passes under it. No if the change is gradual across the boundary.

criterion: A panel in the engagement portal is held in place as the page scrolls past.
evaluation_rule: Yes if any portal panel stays pinned while the rest of the page moves. No if the portal scrolls as an ordinary document.

criterion: The capabilities deck control in the header carries a generic marketing phrase rather than the wording GET CAPABILITIES DECK.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the header control that requests the capabilities deck carries any wording other than GET CAPABILITIES DECK. No if it carries that wording as written.
